title: Restriction of localization presentations to full triangulated subcategories
statement: Let \(\mathcal C\) be a pretriangulated preadditive category with a zero object and additive integer shifts. Let \(S\) be a full triangulated object property of \(\mathcal C\). Let \(P=(F,H,\epsilon,\eta)\) be a presentation [def-sf-recollement-presentation-data], where \(F,H:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C\), \(\epsilon:F\to\mathrm{id}\), and \(\eta:\mathrm{id}\to H\), and assume \(F,H\) carry objects satisfying \(S\) to objects satisfying \(S\). Restrict these literal functors and maps to the full subcategory \(\mathcal C_S\). Additivity and linearity, whenever given on the original functors, restrict. If the original two maps extend to a distinguished triangle at every object, the restricted maps do also. If \(\operatorname{Hom}(F(K)[n],H(M))=0\) for all objects \(K,M\) and integers \(n\), the same vanishing holds in \(\mathcal C_S\).

source.place: Integral sheaf localization and coefficient passage, steps 3–10

proof.text: Lift the given functors and transformations to the full subcategory. Lift the connecting arrow after the inverse inclusion-shift comparison. The inclusion sends the resulting triangle to one isomorphic to the original distinguished triangle. Its fully faithful Hom map and shift isomorphism transfer orthogonality.
